## Open questions

- **L8's bf16 path has to replicate a head permutation, or it is a different
  model.** L3a-3 and vLLM between them: llama.cpp's converter reorders the 48
  V heads from HF's grouped order into tiled order — `in_proj_qkv`'s V rows,
  `in_proj_z`, `in_proj_a`, `in_proj_b`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`, `conv1d`'s V
  channels and `out_proj`'s columns, all seven together — so that `h % 16`
  recovers the right key head. Phase 2's stated alternative is to re-quantise
  "from the 360 GB bf16 (clean — and unsloth publish their imatrix)", and that
  source is in **HF's** order, where `h % 16` is wrong on 32 of the 48 heads.
  It would be wrong in **36 of the 48 layers** with nothing but perplexity to
  notice. Either replicate `_reorder_v_heads` or switch `kHeadOfV` to divide;
  never half of each. Transcoding the GGUF (D1's default) is unaffected.
- ~~**Does the DeltaNet kernel want the scan or the chunk?**~~ **Answered at
  L3b, by pricing rather than by building.** The scan, at the rung this
  hardware wants, is **413 us a layer against the reference's 438** — and it is
  **13% of the layer**, where the fused input projection is 64%. The chunked
  form is 1.15x the arithmetic on the matrix cores: a 4.3x ceiling at §2.7's
  best measured rate, 1.1-1.6x at an honest one for 64x64x128 tiles with a
  serial triangular solve in the middle, and a *perfect* version saves 1.0% of
  the prefill graph while putting a recurrent state through fp16 operands.
  **What is still open is the same question at decode**, where a chunk is a
  token and the whole argument changes; that is L7's.
- **Why is llama.cpp's own scan shape 6.3x better in its kernel than in
  ours?** L3b-3 ran the reference's decomposition — one state column per
  workgroup, 6144 workgroups, q and k re-read 128 times — and got 2766 us
  where llama.cpp's own kernel does 438 at what should be the same work. The
  operand traffic is most of ours (deleting it: 2766 → 1013 us) and the
  subgroup reductions are not (5%), but 1013 is still 2.3x the reference's
  whole dispatch. Ours wins at a different rung and by more than this costs,
  so it is written down rather than chased — but it is the one place in this
  vertical where the reference does something we cannot reproduce.

- ~~**Why is prefill 393 and not ~2000?**~~ **Answered by L2a**: neither
  candidate. It is the hyper-connection block's glue and its `[10240, 4]` F32
  `inject` projection, plus a MoE kernel 2.53x off ours. See L2a above.
- ~~**How much of the 30.6% glue actually fuses?**~~ **L2c answers it for the
  first block** (4.24x on the nameable lines, the optimistic end of L2a's

  gated norm alone). All three dense blocks are in and all three land inside
  that spread. **L5b closes the last of it**: the MoE's own glue — the GLU,

  in, and the whole nameable graph is 87.2% replaced by 61.4%.

description: The whole-model runs (`cmd/llm -resident` and `-graph`, `TestGraphLogits`) stage 84-85 GB of qwen3.8-flash-next; what they cost in time and RAM, and why nothing else can run beside them.

`go run ./cmd/llm -resident` (added 2026-09-16, LLM.md L6a) stages every layer
of all five blocks: **84.20 GB of device buffers, ~35 s wall clock**, and it
ends with about 41 GB of MemAvailable left on this 117.7 GiB machine. Peak
host memory is separate — the dense blocks dequantise to f32 before packing,
and the 36 DeltaNet layers are 8.35 GB of transient floats at once — which is
why the tool stages dense first and the 77 GB expert bank last.

**Why:** it is the only thing in the repo that takes most of the machine, so a
second GPU or large-allocation job started beside it will either fail to
allocate or perturb the timing it prints. `-bank N,N,...` restages just the
bank, which is the cheap way to vary residency; `-dense` is the 6.8 GB half
and runs in 8 s.

`go run ./cmd/llm -graph` and `go test ./llm/ -run TestGraphLogits` (added
2026-09-16, LLM.md L6b) are the same weight but **85.47 GB**, because they add
the 1.27 GB lm head; `-tokens 2048` adds another ~1.1 GB of arenas. Staging is
~35-40 s, so budget a 1800 s timeout. Both take a `-layers 4` / `GraphOpts{
Layers: 4}` prefix that is 7.4 GB and three seconds — use that while changing
anything about the order, and the full stage only for the gate.

**How to apply:** run them in the foreground with a long timeout and nothing
else on the GPU, the way [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] asks. `-resident`'s closing
measurement (layer 3's MoE block) is comparable to `-moe -tokens 512 -iters 10`
only at the same iteration count.

content.text:
The next step in `LLM.md` was **L7 — decode**, and it's done. The model generates.

## What was built

**L7a — the KV cache** (`llm/gpu_attn.go`, the four attention shaders). The query's geometry and the key's part company: `plane` padded token rows against **nKV cells, one plane a layer**, and every causal comparison becomes a cell against a *position*. The indexer needed two things a cache doesn't suggest — its *raw* key cached per cell (a pooled block spans four cells, which at decode arrive in four batches) and its *pooled* table rebuilt only where a block completed, one workgroup instead of 1024.

**L7b — the sequence** (`llm/graph.go`, `shaders/llm_seq_hist.comp`). Five histories carry, and one of them — the DeltaNet's convolution window — turned out to be **shared by all 36 layers**, invisible while every pass was a fresh sequence and 12x wrong at `l_last-1` the moment it wasn't. Both convolutions now read a per-layer ring addressed by absolute position, which makes the store a pure write.

**L7c — the loop** (`llm/sample.go`, `cmd/llm -gen`). Greedy sampling, the end-of-generation set, and the numbers.

## The gates

- A 4096-token prompt through the attention layer in chunks of 512, 64, 7 or **one**: identical to the last place, all 10 485 760 floats.
- The whole graph over 512 tokens in chunks of 128, of 9, or 495-then-seventeen-singles: `result_norm` identical to the last place. Control (every token a fresh sequence): 1.785e+00 rms.
- **The text is llama.cpp's** — same capitals, same `<think>`, same `Lisbon.` — diverging at exactly one token where our top two logits are `"." 25.362` against `" for" 25.201`, 0.161 apart, and re-converging within a sentence.

## Three findings worth flagging

1. **`float(float16_t(x))` is dead code on this driver.** L2e's fp16 key-cache round trip had never actually run on the GPU — the inline cast is bit-identical to no cast, `spirv-dis` shows both `OpFConvert`s surviving, so RADV's NIR folds it. A value that models a memory format has to go through memory.
2. **One `madvise(MADV_RANDOM)` on the n-gram table is worth 176x** on the host gather. Sixteen scattered 90-byte reads drew sixteen 128 KB readahead windows: 2 MB of I/O to deliver 1.41 KB.
3. **The decode ceiling is 25.0 tok/s, not 38.2** — our dense half is staged as halves, so a token reads 9.67 GB not 6.334. That's llama.cpp's measured rate exactly, so the reference is at the ceiling of the bank *it* reads.

## Where it landed

Prefill **950.3 tok/s at ubatch 2048 (2.43x)**, unchanged-to-better. Decode **7.46 tok/s** (two runs 0.27% apart), 30% of this bank's own ceiling. The attribution is specific: the hyper-connection `down` projection at 29 GB/s (336 output columns → ~21 workgroups on 40 CUs) and the MoE padding one token's rows to 32. That's **L7d**, staged in `LLM.md` as a task list rather than a direction.

Write-ups in `research/l7a-kv-cache.md`, `l7b-sequence.md`, `l7c-decode.md`; `LLM.md` and `TODO.md` updated; `results/l7_graph.csv` and `l7c_decode.csv` recorded. Full suite green.
